subject: Globex — adoption is flat, flagging early
body:
Lena —

Globex usage in January was 8% below our adoption target. They're licensed for 410 seats; weekly active is sitting at 215. Renewal is September.

My read: their executive sponsor (Linda Park, COO) hasn't been visible internally since onboarding. James O'Brien (Director IT Ops, our primary contact) is solid but doesn't have the org weight to drive adoption across plant ops.

Proposing: pivot Q1 plan from 'feature deepening' to 'executive-sponsor program'. I'd like to do a working-session QBR with Linda in April (not the standard slide-show QBR), with a real adoption plan agreement on the table. Want your air cover to push for Linda's time.

Will draft the QBR scope this week.

— P

subject: Q1 QBR — proposing a different format
body:
Hi James, Linda,

Quick context: I've been reviewing where we are on adoption — Globex is licensed for 410 seats and currently active around 215. That gap is roughly $110k of value not being realized year over year.

For Q1's QBR I want to propose a different format than slides — a 90-minute working session with the three of us, my VP Lena, and whoever from your team owns plant-floor incident routing. Goal: leave with a concrete adoption plan we both commit to.

If we keep the standard QBR format, I think we'll have a polite review of usage charts and not change the trajectory.

Linda, Lena and I would value 30 minutes of your time on the working session — your involvement will signal that this is a priority.

Proposing April 9 or 10. Calendly: cal.com/priyasharma if easier.

Best,
Priya

title: Globex Q1 QBR — working session
discussion:
Hard conversation but productive.

Adoption gap diagnosis: Mark Tessler revealed something James and Linda didn't know — plant supervisors have been trained on the platform but most still maintain a parallel spreadsheet for incident routing because the spreadsheet was 'what they grew up with'. Adoption isn't a tooling problem, it's a change-management problem.

Linda took ownership: 'this is mine to fix on our side, I should have been visible months ago.'

Real barriers identified: (1) supervisors weren't included in design feedback during rollout, (2) two custom workflows that supervisors NEED don't exist yet (parts-shortage triage, off-hours escalation chain), (3) no internal champion at the supervisor level.

Commitments:
- Globex side: Linda will send all-hands by Apr 18 framing the platform as the canonical incident system. Spreadsheet sunset by May 30.
- Northwind side: Hannah Chen runs a supervisor-feedback session in late April; Diego prioritizes the two missing workflow templates for May.
- Joint: Mark designates two supervisor champions; Priya runs a champions training in May.
decisions: Reset adoption plan: focus on supervisor enablement, not feature breadth

action_items.item: Prioritize parts-shortage triage + off-hours escalation templates

subject: Globex renewal — RFP risk
body:
Lena, Marcus —

New development on Globex. James mentioned in passing today that procurement has issued an RFP that includes a competitor in our space (won't name in writing, but you can guess). This is procurement's standard playbook for renewals over $200k, not a signal of dissatisfaction — but it's not zero risk.

My read:
- Adoption is now at 380/410 seats active. The April QBR worked; spreadsheet sunset hit, supervisors trained.
- Linda is firmly on our side. James is neutral-positive.
- Procurement will press hardest on price.

Proposing: hold pricing flat (no expansion ask this cycle), accept the RFP process, lean on adoption metrics + Linda relationship to win. Marcus — do we have ammunition from the prospect-loss data on the competitor?

— P

title: Globex renewal — final negotiation

transcript_segments.speaker: Diane
transcript_segments.text: I'll start. We've completed the RFP review. Northwind is the recommended vendor. We're prepared to renew, but we'd like to discuss the contract terms, specifically pricing.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Thanks Diane. Glad the RFP came down on the right side. What are the specific terms you want to discuss?

transcript_segments.speaker: Diane
transcript_segments.text: We're looking for a 7% price reduction year over year, justified by the competitive bid we have in hand.

transcript_segments.speaker: Priya
transcript_segments.text: Hear you. Two things — first, Globex is one of our top-quartile accounts on adoption now. That's a flat-renewal story on our side, not a discount story. Second, I'd want to understand what the alternative bid is comparing apples-to-apples — specifically whether SSO, audit retention, and the supervisor workflows are scoped equivalent.

transcript_segments.speaker: Linda
transcript_segments.text: Diane, the RFP was about due diligence. Operations strongly prefers continuity. Priya's right that the alternative wasn't apples-to-apples — they didn't have the off-hours escalation.

transcript_segments.speaker: Diane
transcript_segments.text: Understood. Let me put a different number on the table — flat year-over-year, 12-month commit.

transcript_segments.speaker: Lena
transcript_segments.text: Flat works for us. Diane, I'd offer one thing in lieu of price reduction — we'll co-fund a usage workshop in Q4 with our Solutions team to expand the platform into your supplier-compliance workflow if that's a roadmap priority for Linda.

transcript_segments.speaker: Diane
transcript_segments.text: Then we have an agreement at flat 12-month, with the workshop included. I'll send paper to your desk by Friday.

decisions: Co-funded supplier-compliance workshop in Q4 included in renewal

action_items.item: Send paper to Priya by Friday
Schedule Q4 supplier-compliance workshop with Hannah + Diego
